title: Cisplatin chemoradiation, then paclitaxel and carboplatin
schedule_label: Two cisplatin visits during radiotherapy, then four chemotherapy cycles.
schedule_summary: Usually start 4–6 weeks after surgery. Cisplatin is given before radiation on two treatment days three weeks apart. Ring both teams if radiation is cancelled. Cisplatin is only given on a radiation day. Within three weeks of finishing radiation, start paclitaxel then carboplatin AUC 5, every three weeks for four cycles. Bring your steroid premedication instructions.
purpose: Lower the chance of the cancer returning after surgery.
indication_text: Adjuvant treatment after surgery for high-risk stage I–III endometrial carcinoma.
administration_text: Usually start 4–6 weeks after surgery. Cisplatin is given before radiation on two treatment days three weeks apart. Ring both teams if radiation is cancelled. Cisplatin is only given on a radiation day. Within three weeks of finishing radiation, start paclitaxel then carboplatin AUC 5, every three weeks for four cycles. Bring your steroid premedication instructions.
monitoring_summary: Check recovery, renal function, electrolytes and that radiotherapy will proceed that day.
review_status: Feasibility build. Clinical, pharmacy and patient review pending.

agents.name: Cisplatin
agents.explanation: It damages DNA in dividing cells. It can also affect kidney function, hearing and nerves.
agents.mechanism: It damages DNA in dividing cells. It can also affect kidney function, hearing and nerves.
agents.watch: Report ringing in the ears, hearing loss, reduced urine or new numbness.
visual: It damages DNA in dividing cells. It can also affect kidney function, hearing and nerves.

agents.name: Paclitaxel
agents.explanation: It disrupts cell division. Hair follicles, blood cells and nerves can also be affected.
agents.mechanism: It disrupts cell division. Hair follicles, blood cells and nerves can also be affected.
agents.watch: Report numbness and tell the nurse immediately if you flush or wheeze during treatment.
visual: It disrupts cell division. Hair follicles, blood cells and nerves can also be affected.

agents.name: Carboplatin
agents.explanation: It damages DNA in dividing cells. Kidney function helps determine the prescribed amount.
agents.mechanism: It damages DNA in dividing cells. Kidney function helps determine the prescribed amount.
agents.watch: Report fever, bleeding, hearing changes or an infusion reaction.
visual: It damages DNA in dividing cells. Kidney function helps determine the prescribed amount.

common_effects.title: How you feel between visits
common_effects.text: Tiredness, nausea or appetite changes can make everyday activities harder. Ask your team for help if symptoms interfere with eating or drinking.

serious_effects.title: Hearing changes · Cisplatin
serious_effects.text: Tell the team about ringing or new hearing loss before further cisplatin.

serious_effects.title: Kidney injury · Cisplatin
serious_effects.text: IV fluids help protect the kidneys. Report reduced urine or persistent vomiting urgently.

serious_effects.title: Numb hands or feet · Paclitaxel
serious_effects.text: Report tingling, difficulty fastening buttons or a change in balance before your next dose.

serious_effects.title: Hair loss · Paclitaxel
serious_effects.text: Discuss headwear or scalp cooling with the team before the first infusion.

serious_effects.title: Hearing · Carboplatin
serious_effects.text: Report ringing in your ears or a change in hearing.

questions.q: What happens at my next visit?
questions.a: Two cisplatin visits during radiotherapy, then four chemotherapy cycles.

questions.q: Which symptoms should I phone about?
questions.a: Call your oncology unit urgently for fever, shivering or sudden illness. Report persistent vomiting, reduced urine or severe diarrhoea promptly.

questions.q: What should I plan before starting?
questions.a: Confirm the radiotherapy appointment before travelling.

questions.q: My radiotherapy session was cancelled. Should I still attend for cisplatin?
questions.a: Contact both units before attending. The concurrent cisplatin dose is postponed until radiotherapy resumes. Your later paclitaxel and carboplatin visits follow a separate schedule.

evidence.title: PORTEC-3
evidence.interpretation: Adjuvant chemoradiotherapy improved survival outcomes compared with pelvic radiotherapy alone in the high-risk trial population.
evidence.limitations: Individual benefit depends on stage, pathology and molecular risk. Review the postoperative plan at the multidisciplinary meeting.
